fields.event: About on convoy track, between convoy and "Hole in the Wall" at PORT APRA. Came left and headed toward center of convoy on course 005. Convoy consists of six or seven ships in rough formation of three columns. Five escorts sighted, three of which were CHIDORIS or large PCs leading and on either bow. Several times escorts had doubtful sound contacts on us and shifted to hand keying. Range too great to fire. Convoy then made a large zig to right leaving us on port bow. All tubes ready to fire. Could not swing to port without running afoul of port bow escort who already had a doubtful sound contact. Let escort pass by at about 1,000 yards, swung right to 060 T., and got set-up for stern tubes on 5,000 ton AK in port column.

fields.event: SHIP CONTACT #3 - ATTACK #2 - FIVE HITS. Sighted CHIDORI or PC standing out of harbor. Headed towards.

Made out seven ship convoy standing out of harbor, with four or five escorts including a small freighter type escort trailing. Escorts were milling around, but seemed to be patrolling mostly to northward, indicating convoy was EMPIRE bound and placing us in a favorable position for attack.
Made forward tubes ready. All seven ships appear to be good sized, and one is a four goal poster. Possibly same convoy as sighted yesterday.
Convoy took large zig to southwestward, joining into three columns. Minimum range 3800 yards. Held fire as range was too great. Continued high speed approach hoping for favorable zig.
Secured tubes when range continued to open. Started trailing convoy at high speed submerged.
Sighted a "LILY" bearing 072 T., distance 12 miles. Convoy smoke bears 232 T.
Last bearing of convoy smoke on 213 T. Still a bit too close to GUAM to surface.
Surfaced and started pursuing convoy. GUAM in sight about 30 miles astern, battery well down.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Regained contact with smoke. Closed until head masts in sight with high periscope. With all the planes available at GUAM it seems a miracle this convoy had no air cover. [page 5] At sunset increased speed to gain radar contact. Radar chose this moment to break down, technicians busy. Hydraulic plant motor also picked this time to go out, stood by hand diving stations. Closed target until they could be seen in bright moonlight (full moon) and started end-around run down moon.

flags: The sunset paragraph at the top of page 5 has no time of its own; joined to this entry.

fields.event: Lost contact. Sky had become cloudy and when convoy made large sunset zig we had apparently shifted to a cloud shadow. Started retiring search curve at full speed from convoy's last known position. Hydraulic plant back in commission.
Sighted convoy bearing 080 T., distance about 10 miles. Started end around run. Radar still out.
Radar back in commission. Commenced tracking.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Escort challenged us with an ⟦AA⟧. Convoy range was about 16,000 yards, radar simultaneously picked up an escort at 9,000 yards. Put stern to escort, and increased speed.

fields.event: Two ships in convoy turned on red lights, indicating we were sighted. Convoy had apparently turned away. Heard quite a few explosions, possibly gunfire but probably depth charges as no shell splashes could be seen.
Out of radar contact, turned around and headed toward convoy.
Picked up an escort dead ahead at 14,000 yards.
Escort closing rapidly, changed course to southward and worked around him.
Made contact with convoy bearing 302 T., 29,000 yards. Still in contact with escort working around to southward of him.
Convoy bears 313 T., 26,900 yards. Started another end-around, convoy base course now about 220 T.
Dove for attack with convoy bearing 031 T., 19,400 yards. Commenced submerged approach at periscope depth.
Made bow tubes ready. About dead ahead of convoy, twilight just starting so can see convoy plainly. Convoy in three columns, angle on bow center column zero.

fields.description: Convoy was seen to leave PORT APRA morning of May 9th. Could not close to firing position at this time but convoy was seen to consist of 1 AP similar to TATUHARU MARU and six AK average size of about 5,000 tons. Trailed submerged, surfaced, tracked and attacked convoy just before dawn. Remainder of convoy was turned back and returned to PORT APRA.
fields.sunk: 1 AP similar TATUHARU MARU (ONI 208-J (Rev) p.123) 6,335 tons, 1 AP identified as MIKAGE MARU #18 (ONI 208-J (Rev) p.111 4,319 tons.

When came to periscope depth saw MIKAGE MARU burning and watched it sink. Saw sufficient debris in vicinity to account for two other ships sunk. Convoy was turned back and when seen later could only count three ships, one of which appeared to be damaged.

fields.event: Ship had seemed on verge of sinking all morning, but was still hanging on. Close inspection showed it to be abandoned, called for 4" and 40 MM crew and was about to surface and sink it with gunfire when a "BETTY" (A/C#3) appeared over the horizon and dampened our enthusiasm. Decided to wait a little while longer and if it still didn't sink would ventilate it with a torpedo. Its back was broken and with each swell could see the bow and stern working. Close inspection showed it to check closely with the picture of the MIKAGE MARU #18, 4319 T., ONI 208 J (Revised) p.111.

fields.event: Plane circled target again. Much debris was noted bearing about 235 T., distance about 2 - 4 miles from target, consisting of oil drums, wood, whale boat type lifeboat, etc. Had to duck periscope often to avoid striking it against the heavy debris.

As we were preparing to get a tube ready to finish off target it sank of its own accord, going down bow first. Took pictures. A landing barge (metal) floated off it as ship sank. Sky overcast, remained submerged due to good chance of plane returning.
Surfaced and cruised amongst debris looking for information of intelligence value.
Headed on course 347 T. (last bearing of remnants of convoy) at full speed on three engines.

Made radar contact, bearing 320 T., range 22,000 yards. Believe this to be remnants of convoy which was heading back toward GUAM. Started end-around run, keeping at least 19,000 yards away to avoid detection. Made run around stbd side, skirting GALVEZ BANK. Could count only four pips at this range, which are believed to have been the three freighters and the escort freighter. Convoy tracked at about 6.5 knots, indicating possible damaged ship as previous speed had been higher.

[SUMMARY] Dove 22,000 yards ahead of convoy and began a periscope approach in bright moonlight; leading escort appeared to pick us up by echo ranging and the convoy eased westward. The moon clouded over and the convoy got by before it was light enough to see. 'Should have delayed diving until light conditions were more favorable.' Made out three freighters, smoke from the after hold of one. Remained submerged within sight of GUAM.
Surfaced, set course for next area of PENTATHLON. Started converting #4 into normal fuel tank.

[SUMMARY] Dove for attack with target bearing 160 T., 15,570 yards: a lightly loaded 4,000 ton MFM counter-stern freighter with four escorts (2 DE type, 1 PC, 1 trawler-type escort). Best shot was a bow shot, 120 track, 3500 yards; held fire in the calm sea. A vessel had followed the boat during the end-around at about 19 knots and a submarine was seen astern. The escorts appeared to pick the boat up by sound and put themselves between it and the target; passed within 150 yards of one escort, which did not drop. During the day closed SAIPAN CHANNEL; many SALLYS and ZEKES, no shipping or patrol boats, no evidence of sono-buoys.
Surfaced and patrolled to eastward of SAIPAN.

fields.narrative: [SUMMARY] Let target steady down on a zig toward and fired four bow tubes, gyros near zero, track about 60 stbd, torpedo run 1600 yards. Went deep as an escort was close aboard to port. Heard two timed hits; the first barrage landed as the boat passed 150 feet. Four escorts and planes 'turned to on us with a vengeance', evasion limited by the nearby shore; the escorts made simultaneous runs coached by a fourth pinging abeam. Sixty one charges were dropped, including one salvo of twenty four in rapid succession; possible breaking up noises on the bearing of the attack.

fields.narrative: Fired six tubes forward; firing three at each AK. Fired a little sooner than had planned, as leading escort had started to turn toward, and stbd escort was dead ahead range 2,000 yards. Used one degree diverzcnt spread, torpedo run 3400 yards first torpedo, gyros about 030, track 80 stbd. [page 18] 0135 Heard and saw two hits in each AK, followed by tremendous explosions and flames which lit up the whole scene almost as bright as day. Turned away and went ahead emergency. Escorts closed to 1650 yards and then slowly opened out. Escorts were probably blinded by the holocaust which was now raging astern and added to the confusion by dropping twenty six depth charges. Both AK pips disappeared from the radar screen within three minutes from the time they were hit and it is doubtful that any of the crews survived. Ships were apparently loaded with gasoline and a million or so gallons burning is truly an awe-inspiring spectacle.
